Yet, the rules are simple.

  • Buy good batteries, make sure they are appropriate for your device (max discharge rate is important),
  • make sure there is no tears on the wrap; rewrap them otherwise.
  • If you bring spare batteries with you, store them in a battery case (they're cheap, illumn.com give them with a purchase). It is not a good idea to put them in your pocket full of change.
  • Do not over-discharge (good regulated device have a cutoff), do not over-charge (a good charger will take care of that).
  • If you device takes two or more batteries, buy new batteries and marry them: charge them together and use them together. Never use them separately. Also, buy two (or more) of the same battery, don't mix them because it's pretty.

Here's other things to take in consideration, most of it is common sense: https://batterybro.com/pages/18650-battery-safety

If you have doubt, ask questions. If you don't know why it could blow up in your face, do not buy, use or even consider a mech mod or an unregulated device.
